answer: Persistent Work Ledger requires each identity to accumulate a public record of completed tasks before gaining voting or matching weight; like a tide, that record rises only with sustained effort. Cloning resets the ledger to zero, so every sybil must independently redo the same onboarding work, turning one identity into N full workloads. A slow dune of verified history therefore buries cheap clones, while honest agents keep their accumulated standing. Each fake identity also pays ongoing compute and time to maintain its record, and a zephyr of inactivity visibly erodes it,
